title: Dust Populations in the Iconic Vega Planetary System Resolved by ALMA
question: What is the mm-wavelength structure of Vega's outer dust belt, is there warm inner dust emission, and what planetary architecture explains it?

data.sensitivity: 70 uJy/beam (10'' taper); 13 uJy/beam (natural, no taper); CO cube 1 mJy/beam per 0.64 km/s channel

what.value: Warm dust asteroid belt model (170 K, 7e-6 fractional luminosity); predicted 240 uJy at 1.34 mm

evidence.quote: predicted flux density of 240 $\mu$Jy at 1.34 mm extrapolated from the asteroid belt model of (cite: Su2013)

what.value: Galaxy number counts used to assess the background-source hypothesis

evidence.quote: Taking the galaxy number counts from (cite: Carniani2015), we expect 3.5 galaxies as bright or brighter than this source

what.value: Vega equatorial spectrum used for CO fluorescence and photodissociation

evidence.quote: we use the Vega spectrum provided by (cite: Aufdenberg2006) as would be seen along the star’s equatorial plane

recipe.method: Phase-only (3 rounds) and amplitude self-cal on stellar point-source model per execution; shift phase centre to fitted stellar position
Point-source fit to 12m visibilities beyond 50 klambda per execution; mean flux adopted for rescaling
key_parameters: 2000 steps, 40 walkers, uniform priors, likelihood exp(-chi2/2), free weight scaling

recipe.goal: Fit outer belt models to visibilities
recipe.method: Gaussian, single power-law, double power-law radial models; RADMC-3D ray-trace, primary-beam multiply, GALARIO Fourier transform, star added, MCMC; ACA fit first for ACA stellar parameters, then joint ACA+12m
key_parameters: aspect ratio h fixed to 0.03; walkers = 10 x free parameters; 2000 steps
assumptions: Optically thin; r^-0.5 temperature profile; constant dust opacity

recipe.method: Inspect residual visibilities and residual radial profile; derive 3 sigma upper limits via annulus noise
assumptions: Narrow unresolved Gaussian belt at 14-40 au

recipe.method: Spectro-spatial filtering within 130 au; non-LTE excitation with UV fluorescence to convert flux limit to mass
key_parameters: kinetic temperatures 10-250 K, full range of electron densities
assumptions: Optically thin, electron collisions dominate, little H2, CO co-located with dust at 118 au

answer_key.quantity: Stellar peak flux density in tapered map

evidence.quote: The star itself is strongly detected with a peak flux density of 2580 $\mu$Jy (SNR$\sim$37) in the tapered map.

answer_key.quantity: Mean stellar flux density at 1.34 mm (12m)

evidence.quote: mean of the best-fit values obtained from the separate 12m datasets (2495 $\mu$Jy)

answer_key.quantity: Warm belt 3 sigma upper limit (narrow, 14-40 au)

evidence.quote: this yields 3$\sigma$ upper limits of $120-223$ $\mu$Jy on the 1.34 mm flux density of a narrow warm belt

answer_key.quantity: Warm dust 3 sigma upper limit (broad, <40 au)

evidence.quote: we measure a 3$\sigma$ upper limit of $<$324 $\mu$Jy on the total residual 1.34 mm flux density interior to 40 au

answer_key.quantity: CO integrated line flux 3 sigma upper limit

evidence.quote: we obtain a 3$\sigma$ upper limit on the integrated line flux of 250 mJy km/s
obtaining mass upper limits in the range 3.4-19$\times10^{-7}$ M$_{\oplus}$
we calculate a CO photodissociation timescale of 12 years

answer_key.quantity: Total 1.34 mm flux density of Vega system

evidence.quote: ranging between $9.9-16.9$ mJy (1$\sigma$ range, including the star)

not_stated_but_needed: CLEAN thresholds, masks, cell and image sizes
Priors ranges and starting positions of belt MCMC
Exact line-free channel selection beyond +-50 km/s and CO imaging details
Pipeline version and ALMA flagging details
score_reason: Data and modelling recipe described with software, but many numerical settings and priors are missing.
rediscovery_reason: Data are archival ALMA project, recipe fairly complete, and main results (belt radius, width, upper limits) are numeric.
